t: Nothing remains of this building now, but on Lavender Hill in Battersea there once stood Electric House, an electricity showroom built by Battersea Borough Council. It opened in 1927 and was described as mixing a fin-de-siècle manner with up-to-the-minute Art Deco taste. It was broadly designed by Henry Hyams, a British architect and structural engineer who was also an Esperanto instructor and, in the First World War, a conscientious objector. He is mainly known for two restaurants in Devon and two buildings in Battersea. Electric House was demolished in 1985.
